releases.notes:
One client-only JAR for Minecraft 26.1, 26.1.1, 26.1.2, 26.2, and 26.3.

Install `jsmacros-ruby-1.1.0.jar` alongside the JsMacros Reloaded JAR for your Minecraft version and Fabric Language Kotlin. Existing Ruby scripts and snake_case API usage are unchanged.

This release checks packaged compatibility metadata and has been exercised with an existing Ruby macro framework and its Signs screen on Minecraft 26.3.

releases.notes:
One jar for Minecraft 26.1 through 26.2 (and likely beyond).

jsmacros-ruby never calls into Minecraft directly, only the JsMacros API, so the per-version pin was artificial. This release widens the dependency to `minecraft >=26.1` and drops the Minecraft version from the jar name. Grab `jsmacros-ruby-1.0.2.jar` and it works on any Minecraft that JsMacros Reloaded 2.x supports, including the new 26.2 build.

No code changes.

releases.notes:
Fixes the missing-texture corruption (pink/black checkerboard) that could hit the client after killing a script.

JRuby adopts any thread that runs Ruby code, including the Minecraft render thread when it executes a callback, and that adoption outlives the callback. Closing a script context interrupted every thread the runtime knew about, so the render thread picked up a stray interrupt flag that detonated later in texture and resource loading. The teardown sweep now skips adopted threads; it only interrupts threads the script actually spawned with `Thread.new`, which still die on close.

No API changes. Same requirements as 1.0.0: Minecraft 26.1.2, Fabric, jsmacros 2.x, fabric-language-kotlin.

releases.notes:
Write JsMacros macros in Ruby. Drop a `.rb` file in your JsMacros macros folder and it runs with the full JsMacros API.

JRuby 10.1.0.0 (Ruby 3.4) is bundled in the jar, so there's nothing else to install.

**Requirements**
- Minecraft 26.1.2, Fabric
- jsmacros 2.x
- fabric-language-kotlin

The interop handles Ruby the way you'd expect: callbacks bind to their actual arity, predicates follow Ruby truthiness (`nil` and `false` are false, everything else is true), and an error in a callback keeps its Ruby file and line.

MIT licensed. Client-side only.
